messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: High 5xx rate for Private VPC ILB traffic (cross-region flapping) detected at 2026-03-15T20:01:40Z. Alert rule: private_vpc.ilb.5xx_spike. See: https://alerts.redwood.internal/INC-2026-034

maria: acked. I'm oncall for this window, looking. Noting: customers using Private VPC in EU and US are seeing increased 502/503s.

jon: any obvious infra change in the last hour? deploys? routing changes?

maria: no prod deploys in the last hour from ci. Checking GCP control plane and our ILB configs now.

samir: seeing repeated backend connection resets in logs -> many connections to the ILB IP are hitting different regions. Could be DNS or control-plane route propagation issue at GCP. Dig shows ILB VIP resolving to different regional frontends within TTL window.

maria: copy. running quick checks:
```
# list forwarding rules for private ilbs
gcloud compute forwarding-rules list --filter="name~'private-ilb-.*'" --format="table(name, IPAddress, region)"
# dig on entrypoint
dig +short ilb-service.prod.private.redwood.internal
```

maria: dig output: 10.128.12.7 and 10.132.44.9 alternating on subsequent resolves (same TTL). Not normal.

jon: that smells like GCP LB control-plane flapping or global route fanout got noisy. Have we observed any GCP incident?

gcp-support-bot: Created GCP ticket CR-12345 for "Internal LB VIP cross-region map instability" and routed to Networking team (P0). GCP has acknowledged increased control-plane churn in a limited subset of customers.

katie: pinging support to assemble customer-impact list. Which customers are on Private VPC ILB and are seeing errors?

oncall-eu: receiving pages from 3 customer SREs (alpha-platform, fintech-ops, docs-sync). Latency spikes ~200-800ms and 502s for API calls that traverse ILB.

alex: mitigation proposal: 1) steer traffic to regional fallback ILB endpoints we control, 2) temporarily route egress through nat-shared to avoid the unstable control-plane mapping, 3) communicate RCA draft to affected customers. Which is highest priority?

maria: step 1 first. I'll carve a canary route to prefer us-west1/eu-west1 zonal ILBs. Applying Smart Router override now (10% -> 100% for fallback). Command I used: 
```
# traffic-ops: promote fallback ILB
traffic-ops set-policy --service ilb-service --prefer-region eu-west1 --weight 100
```

jon: watched the change. Backend error rate dropped ~40% in the first 90s for the canary subset. Good sign.

samir: also toggled session affinity to CLIENT_IP on the backend service to reduce cross-region backend churn while GCP stabilizes.

maria: created temporary firewall rule and route to ensure the fallback path stays internal-only. Command: 
```
gcloud compute routes create route-ilb-fallback --network=private-vpc --next-hop-ilb=projects/.../regions/eu-west1/forwardingRules/fallback-ilb --priority=1000
```

gcp-support-bot: GCP Networking L3 suggests keeping traffic on a single regional frontend until control-plane churn resolves; ETA unknown. They recommended failing traffic to zonal ILBs as a short-term mitigation.

katie: drafting status update to impacted customers (alpha-platform, fintech-ops, docs-sync). Will note that we have applied regional failover and are monitoring, no data exfil observed, and we are in touch with GCP.

oncall-eu: status on our side — SLO alerting triggered, but no sustained data loss. Customers reporting degraded availability on a minority of requests.

maria: posted an incident channel timeline in the incident ticket:
- 20:01 UTC: alert fired (ILB 5xx spike)
- 20:03 UTC: oncall ack and triage started
- 20:06 UTC: GCP ticket CR-12345 opened and acknowledged
- 20:10 UTC: traffic-ops regional failover applied (canary -> full for affected services)
- 20:14 UTC: backend affinity set and route priority updated
- 20:25 UTC: error rate down ~70% for canary groups

jon: do we need to escalate internal execs or sales for big customers?

katie: notified sales ops; request from fintech-ops for a war room link. I'll include the warroom and timeline.

samir: implemented a NAT gateway fallback for egress to avoid any GCP ILB control-plane dependent routing for certain healthcheck paths:
```
gcloud compute routers nats update nat-shared --router=shared-router --nat-external-ip-pool=primary --enable-logging
```

maria: please note we should not flip everything to NAT fallback — only healthcheck and control traffic. We'll keep customer traffic on internal path where possible.

gcp-support-bot: GCP update: Investigating control-plane mapping instability, currently affecting a subset of internal LBs in multi-region projects. Next update in 15m.

alex: timeline and handoff: I will take ownership of monitoring and customer comms for the next 2 hours. maria, please handoff any remaining network tasks.

maria: handing off to alex at 20:48 UTC — all active mitigations applied, runbook steps completed up to 'monitor until stable'. Notes attached: {traffic-ops change-id: to-4592, gcp-cr: CR-12345, routes: route-ilb-fallback}.

jon: one more ask — capture packet captures (pcap) or tcpdump on the affected backends for root-cause. Samir, can you run short tcpdump and upload?

samir: running tcpdump now on a backend host for 120s and uploading to /var/tmp/ilb-pcaps/ilb-flap-20-50.pcap. Link: https://artifacts.redwood.internal/ilb-pcaps/ilb-flap-20-50.pcap

katie: customer update posted to alpha-platform and fintech-ops: "We detected intermittent 5xx errors affecting Private VPC ILB routing. We applied a regional failover and are working with GCP. Expect periodic updates every 30 minutes. If you see anything urgent, reply in this thread or open a support ticket."

gcp-support-bot: GCP message: Investigating internal config propagation; can confirm we see transient mapping duplicates across regions. No ETA. Recommend customers keep regionalized frontends until control-plane fully converges.

alex: next steps before we close the active page: 1) keep the regional failover in place and monitor for 60m, 2) collect PCAPs and healthcheck logs for postmortem, 3) coordinate with GCP on RCA and timeline, 4) prepare draft postmortem and customer-facing RCA.

maria: agree. I'll mark the incident as mitigated for paging (error rate under threshold) but keep this channel open for monitoring and the formal postmortem. Marking INC-2026-034 as MITIGATED->MONITOR.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-034 status updated to MITIGATED (paging suspended) at 2026-03-15T20:14:50Z. Next update expected in 30m.

oncall-eu: acknowledged handoff to alex. I'll remain available for customer escalations.

katie: will run comms cadence and notify legal/sales for any contractual impact requests.

jon: thanks team. Postmortem checklist: timeline, root cause hypothesis (GCP control-plane mapping instability), mitigations applied, follow-ups (automate regional failover playbook, add traffic-ops guardrails, more robust healthcheck path via NAT fallback), and customer RCA draft.

maria: saving notes and runbook changes to docs: https://docs.redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-034-notes.md

alex: closing loop. If error rate rises again, repage page-sre and re-open this channel. Otherwise we'll convert into a postmortem thread in 24h.

katie: thanks all — customer updates will continue every 30m until fully resolved. :thumbsup:
